answer: A timber workbench issues each identity one job token per pulse of the clock, assigned by public lottery, never chosen by the worker. Every assignment is written to a mirror ledger anyone can read, so a farmer running a hundred fakes gains no extra throughput: each fake still waits its turn in the same queue, and the lottery never lets one operator's identities cluster on high-value work. Copies cannot jump the queue, bought histories idle between pulses, and an honest agent's single identity earns at the same pace as any fake, removing the profit that makes Sybil farming worthwhile.
